# AI Kanban — Browser Workspace for Human-AI Work

## 1. Architecture and Board Workspace lifecycle

Build a polished, dependency-light static JavaScript application deployable to GitHub Pages under `outputs/implementations/ai-kanban-browser/`. It is a local, folder-backed Kanban workspace for human–AI collaboration, not a backend service. Ship semantic HTML, modern CSS, ES modules, relative asset URLs, and checked-in deployable assets. Do not use Node.js at runtime, server routes, serverless functions, WebSockets, or a separately installed local service. The deployable root contains `index.html`; it must work from a repository subpath.

The useful core works without an AI provider: users create and organize cards, edit plans, preserve activity and outputs, use agent handoff packets, and retain a portable Board Workspace. A workspace folder is the local trust, portability, and collaboration boundary. It contains `board.sqlite`, a versioned manifest, managed bootstrap files, attachments, artifacts, exports, and private coordination files. The app must neither read nor write outside the user-authorized root, modify unrecognized files, execute workspace content, nor upload workspace bytes for analytics, diagnostics, previews, or crash reporting.

First run presents three honest choices: **Open Board Workspace**, **Create Board Workspace**, and **Try demo**. Try demo offers a visually preferred **Create a real demo workspace**, using normal folder validation, managed agent bootstrap, and a seeded Personal Research board; and **Try in memory**, which creates no folder, disables local-agent integration, and requires export to retain changes. When folder access is unsupported, explain why only memory/import-download flows are available. Before Open, Create, Try demo, reconnect, or Close replaces dirty state, require Save or confirmation; cancellation changes nothing. Closing clears in-memory domain state and offers portable export.

On supported secure-context Chromium browsers, invoke `showDirectoryPicker()` only from a user gesture, request read/write permission from a user gesture, and persist `FileSystemDirectoryHandle` in IndexedDB only for recent-workspace reconnection. On return, query permission and request it again only from a gesture. Show folder name, permission mode, dirty/saving/saved/conflict state, and last durable write; never imply persistence without a writable handle. Feature-detect File System Access API. Unsupported browsers use explicit archive import/export and are labelled import/download rather than connected autosave.

Use a manifest with workspace id, format and protocol versions, primary state file, reserved directories, owned files, bootstrap paths and fingerprints. Fixed paths include `board.sqlite`, `manifest.json`, `attachments/`, `artifacts/`, `exports/`, and `.ai-kanban/coordination/`. Validate every path against the workspace root and reject absolute paths, `..`, symlink escapes, directory targets, and unknown external references. Treat imported files, agent changes, attachments, packets, and generated output as untrusted data.

The default Personal Research board has ordered columns `inbox`, `planning`, `in_progress`, `review`, `blocked`, and `done`, displayed as Inbox, Planning, In Progress, Review, Blocked, and Done. Seed examples for a macroeconomic pulse, activities with a four-year-old in São Paulo, family trips, a collaborative vacation planner, and other age-appropriate activities. Users can create, edit, archive, search, filter, reorder, and move cards through pointer and keyboard controls.

Run SQLite in a dedicated Web Worker using a pinned, vendored SQLite WASM distribution. The worker owns the sole live connection and exposes a validated message-based repository API; UI code never receives a raw database handle or issues SQL. Import `board.sqlite` from `Uint8Array` and export complete database bytes after committed mutations. In-memory SQLite, OPFS, IndexedDB, and caches are working state only; `board.sqlite` is canonical. Document a practical workspace-size limit because saves rewrite the full database, while keeping the main thread responsive.

## 2. SQLite schema and repository operations

Enable foreign keys, rollback-journal mode, full synchronous durability, bounded busy timeout, deterministic transactional migrations, and schema-version checks. Reject future schema versions without changing original bytes; preserve original bytes before migration. Store stable text ids, integer ordering keys, UTC ISO 8601 timestamps with offsets, and integer smallest units for any monetary values. Client-generated timestamps must identify their actor and clock source; no server-authoritative time is claimed. Parameterize all SQL and validate every worker message and repository input.

Implement at minimum these tables and indexed relations:

- `workspace_meta(key, value, updated_at)` for schema version, workspace revision, control generation, owner, and format metadata.
- `boards(id, name, description, created_at, updated_at, archived_at)` and `board_columns(id, board_id, key, name, description, position, archived_at)` with unique `(board_id, key)` and `(board_id, position)`.
- `cards(id, board_id, column_id, kind, title, description_markdown, priority, assignee, attention_state, workflow_phase, position, created_at, updated_at, archived_at, last_change_actor, last_reviewed_revision, revision)`; index board/column/position, updated time, assignee, priority, attention, and searchable title/description.
- `card_dependencies(card_id, depends_on_card_id, relation, created_at)` with foreign keys and duplicate prevention.
- `plan_items(id, card_id, turn_id, text, state, position, created_at, updated_at, completed_at)`; states are explicit and validated.
- `execution_turns(id, card_id, number, status, trigger, requester, assigned_actor, agent_run_id, idempotency_key, source_card_revision, instruction_snapshot, queued_at, claimed_at, started_at, updated_at, completed_at, final_summary, error_details, memory_read_lineage, memory_write_lineage, supersedes_turn_id)` with unique `(card_id, number)` and scoped idempotency protection. Status is one of `queued`, `claimed`, `running`, `needs_input`, `review`, `complete`, `failed`, or `cancelled`.
- `decision_threads(id, card_id, phase, brief_snapshot, selected_option_id, active_turn_id, created_at, updated_at)` and append-only `decision_entries` for briefs, proposals, rankings, feedback, questions, answers, gates, selections, and cancellations. Phases are `briefing`, `exploring`, `needs_feedback`, `committed`, `deep_work`, `review`, and `accepted`.
- `outputs(id, card_id, turn_id, version, type, title, content_or_ref, schema_version, status, source, artifact_path, provenance_json, created_at, updated_at, supersedes_output_id)` for `text`, `status`, `link`, `program`, `table`, `diff`, `image`, and `file` surfaces. Index card/turn/version and status.
- `research_memory(id, card_id, fingerprint, normalized_subject, claim_summary, source_url, publisher, evidence_date, first_seen_cycle, last_seen_cycle, content_hash, relevance, state, lineage_output_id)` and `coverage_ledger` for source families, searches, dates, and access gaps. Memory state is `current`, `updated`, `superseded`, `dismissed`, or `uncertain`.
- append-only `activity_events(id, board_id, card_id, turn_id, type, actor_kind, actor_id, timestamp, summary, payload_json, visibility, correlation_id, revision)`; index card/time, turn/time, actor, type, and errors.
- `agent_records`, `coordination_audit`, `idempotency_records`, and managed-file fingerprints needed for the coordination protocol.

Provide create, open, health, migration, snapshot/query, mutation, export, close, and conflict-recovery repository operations. Every mutation returns an updated domain snapshot or precise change record and marks the connected file dirty. Serialize writes through one save queue; coalesce edits without losing the final state, and make Save flush immediately. Before replacement, compare on-disk revision and content fingerprint to the last-read signature. Unexpected changes abort the save and require reload or explicit conflict recovery. Keep previous bytes until replacement closes successfully; failed or cancelled writes remain dirty and recoverable. Use Web Locks plus `BroadcastChannel` where available; a second tab is read-only unless it holds the workspace lock.

Card movement or reorder and its activity insertion occur in one SQLite transaction. Completing or failing a turn, changing the parent projection, moving a card, and writing final activity also occur in one transaction. Validate allowed transitions and surface a visible reason for invalid moves. The application exposes no HTTP API endpoints; its only durable domain interface is the worker repository contract and the documented workspace/skill CLI protocol.

## 3. Human-agent coordination and skill protocol

Create or repair a versioned managed bootstrap in each connected workspace: root `AGENTS.md`, root `CLAUDE.md`, and canonical `.agents/skills/ai-kanban/` containing `SKILL.md`, a dependency-free Python 3 CLI, and thin POSIX shell and PowerShell launchers. Root files point to the canonical skill rather than duplicating its protocol. Record protocol version, generated paths, and fingerprints in the manifest. Never silently overwrite user-created or user-edited managed files: compare, explain, and require confirmation; update only recognized generated files or explicitly approved managed sections.

After create or reopen, show Start your agent guidance: open a terminal in the Board Workspace and launch Copilot CLI, Claude Code, or another compatible agent. Do not fabricate a `cd` command because directory handles do not reveal portable absolute paths. Show Waiting for agent until a valid workspace-matched heartbeat arrives, then calmly show identity, control state, current turn, and heartbeat time. If absent, provide copyable fallback instructions, diagnostics, Repair agent setup, and retry. Do not promise every product/version discovers root instructions.

The skill is provider-neutral and uses only Python 3 standard library modules, including `sqlite3`, `argparse`, JSON, and filesystem APIs. It preflights Python and required modules; if unavailable, it states the exact trusted installation command and obtains approval before changing the machine. It exposes validated commands for workspace status, ready-work inspection, atomic claim/release, typed mutations, artifact publication, structured questions, answer consumption, yield, heartbeat, and watch. Mutating commands require expected revision, control generation, actor, run id, and idempotency key. Conflicts, revoked control, malformed data, and invalid transitions are explicit failures.

Use `.ai-kanban/coordination/` as a mailbox, not a second domain database. It contains a versioned human signal and one versioned state file per approved agent. Each actor solely writes its own file; all may read. Records include `workspace_id`, protocol version, actor/holder id, monotonic sequence or control generation, timestamp, requested state, and last observed durable revision. Safely replace records; ignore incomplete, stale, mismatched-workspace, or lower-generation records. Keep substantive questions, answers, progress, outputs, and audit history in SQLite.

Enforce a single acknowledged primary-file writer. Model `human`, `granting_agent`, `agent`, `reclaim_requested`, and `recovering`, with `owner`, `holder_id`, `control_generation`, `workspace_revision`, and bounded lease metadata in both SQLite and the mailbox. Every mutation rechecks generation, holder, and expected revision immediately before write. Control changes require request and acknowledgement. A requester does not write until the prior owner commits or rolls back, closes its writer, publishes its final revision, and acknowledges handoff. Human reclaim has priority: the agent completes or rolls back its short transaction, rejects later mutations, publishes yielded, and rereads before a new grant. Lease expiry is recovery evidence, never authorization to overwrite.

For direct native SQLite agent coordination, the browser flushes pending work, increments generation, grants control in SQLite, closes the writable stream, publishes grant, and becomes read-only. Before every agent mutation, open a fresh connection, use `BEGIN IMMEDIATE`, verify control/revision in both locations, mutate plus audit event, increment revision, commit, and close. Never hold a transaction during reasoning, tool execution, artifact generation, waiting, or polling. After commit, publish revision; the browser waits for journal stabilization, runs integrity check, confirms revision, reloads, and preserves selection, scroll, open detail, and unsaved drafts or flags conflicts.

The generated operating loop is explicit: poll with bounded backoff, heartbeat, atomically claim one ready turn, execute through skill commands, publish checkpoints, ask for input or complete/yield, and return to watching while the host runtime remains alive. Empty queues are quiet, not completion. A watch command is opt-in, cancellable, resumable, machine-readable, non-busy-waiting, and immediately yields on reclaim. State plainly that a skill cannot keep a terminated host runtime alive, consume future output, or initiate new model turns; where host hooks/schedulers are unavailable, watch is observation only with manual-resume guidance.

## 4. Cards, decision loops, execution turns, memory, and output surfaces

Cards are operational workspaces, not merely tickets. At creation require a title, board, column, and kind; support task, question, and result presentation. Include Markdown description, priority `P0`–`P3`, assignee, timestamps, attention state, workflow projection, dependencies, provenance, artifact paths, and last-change actor. Compact cards show title, high-value summary, priority, owner, current turn/status, latest-result preview, attention cue, and accessible actions; detail shows all metadata, history, plans, outputs, memory, provenance, and activity. Agent-changed cards show calm violet/teal plus icon and text until reviewed; Needs you uses amber plus icon and text.

Support creation, edit, duplicate where useful, archive, search, filter, sort, saved views, bulk selection, keyboard movement, pointer drag/drop, accessible drop targets, cancellation, optimistic rollback, and useful empty states. Every column has stable id, display name, order, and optional description. Surface board counts, attention, blocked, aging, WIP, ownership, and bottleneck information only when it helps decisions; avoid an operations-console aesthetic.

A turn is one bounded execution attempt against durable card intent. Claim at most one active turn per card by default, atomically with revision and idempotency validation. Initial cards may be Ready for agent and must not execute merely because a template loads. Run again/Requeue creates a fresh queued turn with new id and number, current instruction snapshot, and link to the prior successful turn; it never rewrites earlier turns. Moving completed work to Inbox confirms **Run again** and invokes this same operation. A turn needing input remains active and resumes after an answer; cancellation retains partial outputs, activity, and reason.

Each generated output belongs to a turn and has version, status, timestamps, actor, provenance, optional artifact path, and typed renderer. Render Markdown safely; show programs with language/file/copy actions, tables with schema validation/filter/export, diffs with comparison and approval, images with preview/zoom/download/alt text/provenance, files with safe open/download, and status surfaces with meaningful progress/health. Streamed output is visibly partial; failed/stale/superseded output explains recovery. Feature the latest successful result with preview, age, and Open; keep dated versions in ordered History and support turn comparison when meaningful.

The vacation decision loop is a required exemplar and product flow. In Inbox, the human edits candidate destinations and constraints. In Planning, an exploratory turn researches broad credible alternatives and produces a bounded comparison with fit, evidence, tradeoffs, uncertainty, practical constraints, and distinctions. It asks focused questions rather than guessing consequential preferences, preserves append-only rankings/shortlists/rejections/restorations/annotations, and on later passes identifies materially changed facts and ranking deltas. A deep-research gate requires explicit selected option, current constraints, and a labelled action. A confirmed Planning-to-In Progress move may atomically complete exploration and queue deep work. Deep work snapshots selection, constraints, unresolved questions, evidence, and feedback; it does not silently reconsider rejected options. It produces dated itineraries and decision-specific artifacts, then moves to Review for approval or revision. Acceptance preserves all prior proposals, feedback, turns, outputs, and provenance.

For recurring research cards, every cycle records date, cadence, lookback, exact topic, news/events mode, new findings, still-important context, source coverage, and gaps. Before a cycle, inspect prior reports and visible durable memory. Classify items as new, materially updated, unchanged context, duplicate coverage, corrected, or no longer current; distinguish confirmed fact, reported claim, announcement, opinion, forecast, and speculation. Persist only committed source-backed memory changes with lineage. Let users inspect, search, correct, dismiss, pin, export, and explicitly forget memory; forgetting changes future comparison context but not immutable reports.

## 5. Interface states and interactions

The experience is calm, capable, and trustworthy: restrained navy, mineral teal, warm paper, and coral attention accents; no global chat pane or dense operations console. Use native accessible controls, semantic landmarks, visible keyboard focus, sufficient contrast, screen-reader labels for icon-only controls, reduced-motion support, and responsive layouts down to 320 CSS pixels. The native `hidden` attribute is authoritative and CSS must not reveal inactive states.

Before activation, show Open/Create actions. Once active, show Save, New card, Agent control, AI handoff, Workspace menu, search, attention filters, folder/permission/save state, and Close workspace. Foreground Needs you, AI working, and AI updated counts without overwhelming board scanning. Provide first-run, loading, empty, active, dirty, saving, saved, conflict, unsupported-browser, permission-limited, migration, corrupt-file, recovery, and offline/static-host states with concrete next actions.

Card detail supports metadata/description editing, plan items, outputs, turns, research memory, version history, activity/provenance, structured replies to agent questions, Run again, archive, and publication of polished result cards. Activity entries are compact for routine events and expandable for decisions/errors/output updates; distinguish human, agent, system, automation, and errors calmly, show relative plus exact time, permit filters and copyable/linkable references, and avoid secrets or raw internal payloads.

AI handoff exports selected work as a compact versioned JSON and Markdown packet containing intent, constraints, plan, relevant activity, output shape, and provenance. Users copy/download it for any assistant, then import responses through paste/file selection. Validate a packet fully before preview; require approval for proposed plan, output, status, and activity changes; retain packet plus committed provenance. An optional `AIProviderAdapter` is replaceable and provider-neutral. Credentials are session-memory only, never persisted in browser storage, logs, URLs, analytics, or workspace files. Before send, disclose provider, endpoint, model, exact selected content, and purpose; require confirmation. Network failures leave the workspace unchanged with a retryable draft.

## 6. Security, compatibility, and recovery

All workspace and imported content is untrusted. Safely render Markdown and AI text; never treat it as HTML, scripts, or instructions. Validate manifests, SQLite messages, packet schemas, agent coordination records, artifact paths, external responses, and SQL parameters. External network activity requires a user action and visible destination, purpose, progress, failure, and retry state. The app does not promise secure secret storage, background execution, multi-user coordination, or autonomous service behavior in a static deployment.

Handle permission revocation, missing files, unsupported future manifests/schema, corrupt databases, partial exports, migration failure, lock failure, agent crash, stale signals, expired leases, journal residue, external mutation, agent commit without marker, and browser save conflict with specific recovery guidance. Forced recovery invalidates generation, waits for database/journal stabilization, validates integrity, explains risk, and never silently overwrites. Preserve active form drafts across reloads; present merge/reload choices when conflicts affect them.

Autosave is available only for connected supporting browsers. Elsewhere, explicit archive export/import is the persistence path. Do not silently fall back from a connected workspace to unrelated OPFS or browser storage. Keep all required JavaScript and WASM assets local and version-pinned; core behavior must not depend on mutable CDN assets.

## 7. File tree, implementation sequence, and test matrix

Deliver at least this tree:

```text
outputs/implementations/ai-kanban-browser/
  index.html
  styles.css
  src/
    app.js
    ui/ board/ cards/ detail/ handoff/
    domain/ repositories/ workspace/ coordination/
    worker/sqlite-worker.js
  vendor/sqlite-wasm/
  .agents/skills/ai-kanban/
    SKILL.md
    ai_kanban.py
    ai-kanban.sh
    ai-kanban.ps1
  templates/AGENTS.md
  templates/CLAUDE.md
  sample-workspace/
  tests/unit/
  tests/e2e/
  README.md
  docs/
```

Implement in this order: establish static shell and accessible responsive state model; vendor and validate SQLite WASM worker/repository; implement manifest, folder lifecycle, save queue, locking, export/import, and recovery; migrate schema and seed sample workspace; build board/card/detail/typed-output/activity interfaces; implement turns, decisions, research memory, and transaction rules; add managed agent bootstrap, Python CLI, mailbox/control handoff, and watch behavior; add AI packet handoff/provider adapter boundaries; complete docs, Pages deployment, and verification.

README documents local development and test commands, canonical data boundary, browser support, static-host constraints, workspace-size guidance, known limitations, and agent-host autonomy boundary. Include source, compiled specification, and tutorial links in a quiet footer.

Unit-test schema creation, reopen, migrations, rollback, ordering, archive/deletion rules, worker validation/errors, export/reimport equivalence, corrupt input, future-schema rejection, search/filter, movement/activity atomicity, turn claim/requeue/idempotency, output history, decision gates, memory classifications, path validation, save conflicts, and coordination parsing. Use Playwright for first-run choices, folder-supported and unsupported paths, keyboard drag alternatives, 320-pixel layout, static-host/offline behavior, permission loss, dirty-state confirmation, archive import/export, handoff approval, and no uncaught page or unexpected console errors/warnings. Test browser-to-agent and agent-to-browser handoff, reclaim during work, stale generations, revision conflicts, duplicate keys, crash points before/after commit, journal stabilization, watcher restart/cancellation, unsupported hosts, and two agents attempting to claim the same turn. The build is complete only when users can trust visible board state to match durable state, recover from failures without silent loss, and implementers can execute this test matrix successfully.

# AI Kanban — Browser Workspace for Human-AI Work

## 1. Architecture and Board Workspace lifecycle

Build a polished, dependency-light static JavaScript application deployable to GitHub Pages under `outputs/implementations/ai-kanban-browser/`. It is a local, folder-backed Kanban workspace for human–AI collaboration, not a backend service. Ship semantic HTML, modern CSS, ES modules, relative asset URLs, and checked-in deployable assets. Do not use Node.js at runtime, server routes, serverless functions, WebSockets, or a separately installed local service. The deployable root contains `index.html`; it must work from a repository subpath.

The useful core works without an AI provider: users create and organize cards, edit plans, preserve activity and outputs, use agent handoff packets, and retain a portable Board Workspace. A workspace folder is the local trust, portability, and collaboration boundary. It contains `board.sqlite`, a versioned manifest, managed bootstrap files, attachments, artifacts, exports, and private coordination files. The app must neither read nor write outside the user-authorized root, modify unrecognized files, execute workspace content, nor upload workspace bytes for analytics, diagnostics, previews, or crash reporting.

First run presents three honest choices: **Open Board Workspace**, **Create Board Workspace**, and **Try demo**. Try demo offers a visually preferred **Create a real demo workspace**, using normal folder validation, managed agent bootstrap, and a seeded Personal Research board; and **Try in memory**, which creates no folder, disables local-agent integration, and requires export to retain changes. When folder access is unsupported, explain why only memory/import-download flows are available. Before Open, Create, Try demo, reconnect, or Close replaces dirty state, require Save or confirmation; cancellation changes nothing. Closing clears in-memory domain state and offers portable export.

On supported secure-context Chromium browsers, invoke `showDirectoryPicker()` only from a user gesture, request read/write permission from a user gesture, and persist `FileSystemDirectoryHandle` in IndexedDB only for recent-workspace reconnection. On return, query permission and request it again only from a gesture. Show folder name, permission mode, dirty/saving/saved/conflict state, and last durable write; never imply persistence without a writable handle. Feature-detect File System Access API. Unsupported browsers use explicit archive import/export and are labelled import/download rather than connected autosave.

Use a manifest with workspace id, format and protocol versions, primary state file, reserved directories, owned files, bootstrap paths and fingerprints. Fixed paths include `board.sqlite`, `manifest.json`, `attachments/`, `artifacts/`, `exports/`, and `.ai-kanban/coordination/`. Validate every path against the workspace root and reject absolute paths, `..`, symlink escapes, directory targets, and unknown external references. Treat imported files, agent changes, attachments, packets, and generated output as untrusted data.

The default Personal Research board has ordered columns `inbox`, `planning`, `in_progress`, `review`, `blocked`, and `done`, displayed as Inbox, Planning, In Progress, Review, Blocked, and Done. Seed examples for a macroeconomic pulse, activities with a four-year-old in São Paulo, family trips, a collaborative vacation planner, and other age-appropriate activities. Users can create, edit, archive, search, filter, reorder, and move cards through pointer and keyboard controls.

Run SQLite in a dedicated Web Worker using a pinned, vendored SQLite WASM distribution. The worker owns the sole live connection and exposes a validated message-based repository API; UI code never receives a raw database handle or issues SQL. Import `board.sqlite` from `Uint8Array` and export complete database bytes after committed mutations. In-memory SQLite, OPFS, IndexedDB, and caches are working state only; `board.sqlite` is canonical. Document a practical workspace-size limit because saves rewrite the full database, while keeping the main thread responsive.

## 2. SQLite schema and repository operations

Enable foreign keys, rollback-journal mode, full synchronous durability, bounded busy timeout, deterministic transactional migrations, and schema-version checks. Reject future schema versions without changing original bytes; preserve original bytes before migration. Store stable text ids, integer ordering keys, UTC ISO 8601 timestamps with offsets, and integer smallest units for any monetary values. Client-generated timestamps must identify their actor and clock source; no server-authoritative time is claimed. Parameterize all SQL and validate every worker message and repository input.

Implement at minimum these tables and indexed relations:

- `workspace_meta(key, value, updated_at)` for schema version, workspace revision, control generation, owner, and format metadata.
- `boards(id, name, description, created_at, updated_at, archived_at)` and `board_columns(id, board_id, key, name, description, position, archived_at)` with unique `(board_id, key)` and `(board_id, position)`.
- `cards(id, board_id, column_id, kind, title, description_markdown, priority, assignee, attention_state, workflow_phase, position, created_at, updated_at, archived_at, last_change_actor, last_reviewed_revision, revision)`; index board/column/position, updated time, assignee, priority, attention, and searchable title/description.
- `card_dependencies(card_id, depends_on_card_id, relation, created_at)` with foreign keys and duplicate prevention.
- `plan_items(id, card_id, turn_id, text, state, position, created_at, updated_at, completed_at)`; states are explicit and validated.
- `execution_turns(id, card_id, number, status, trigger, requester, assigned_actor, agent_run_id, idempotency_key, source_card_revision, instruction_snapshot, queued_at, claimed_at, started_at, updated_at, completed_at, final_summary, error_details, memory_read_lineage, memory_write_lineage, supersedes_turn_id)` with unique `(card_id, number)` and scoped idempotency protection. Status is one of `queued`, `claimed`, `running`, `needs_input`, `review`, `complete`, `failed`, or `cancelled`.
- `decision_threads(id, card_id, phase, brief_snapshot, selected_option_id, active_turn_id, created_at, updated_at)` and append-only `decision_entries` for briefs, proposals, rankings, feedback, questions, answers, gates, selections, and cancellations. Phases are `briefing`, `exploring`, `needs_feedback`, `committed`, `deep_work`, `review`, and `accepted`.
- `outputs(id, card_id, turn_id, version, type, title, content_or_ref, schema_version, status, source, artifact_path, provenance_json, created_at, updated_at, supersedes_output_id)` for `text`, `status`, `link`, `program`, `table`, `diff`, `image`, and `file` surfaces. Index card/turn/version and status.
- `research_memory(id, card_id, fingerprint, normalized_subject, claim_summary, source_url, publisher, evidence_date, first_seen_cycle, last_seen_cycle, content_hash, relevance, state, lineage_output_id)` and `coverage_ledger` for source families, searches, dates, and access gaps. Memory state is `current`, `updated`, `superseded`, `dismissed`, or `uncertain`.
- append-only `activity_events(id, board_id, card_id, turn_id, type, actor_kind, actor_id, timestamp, summary, payload_json, visibility, correlation_id, revision)`; index card/time, turn/time, actor, type, and errors.
- `agent_records`, `coordination_audit`, `idempotency_records`, and managed-file fingerprints needed for the coordination protocol.

Provide create, open, health, migration, snapshot/query, mutation, export, close, and conflict-recovery repository operations. Every mutation returns an updated domain snapshot or precise change record and marks the connected file dirty. Serialize writes through one save queue; coalesce edits without losing the final state, and make Save flush immediately. Before replacement, compare on-disk revision and content fingerprint to the last-read signature. Unexpected changes abort the save and require reload or explicit conflict recovery. Keep previous bytes until replacement closes successfully; failed or cancelled writes remain dirty and recoverable. Use Web Locks plus `BroadcastChannel` where available; a second tab is read-only unless it holds the workspace lock.

Card movement or reorder and its activity insertion occur in one SQLite transaction. Completing or failing a turn, changing the parent projection, moving a card, and writing final activity also occur in one transaction. Validate allowed transitions and surface a visible reason for invalid moves. The application exposes no HTTP API endpoints; its only durable domain interface is the worker repository contract and the documented workspace/skill CLI protocol.

## 3. Human-agent coordination and skill protocol

Create or repair a versioned managed bootstrap in each connected workspace: root `AGENTS.md`, root `CLAUDE.md`, and canonical `.agents/skills/ai-kanban/` containing `SKILL.md`, a dependency-free Python 3 CLI, and thin POSIX shell and PowerShell launchers. Root files point to the canonical skill rather than duplicating its protocol. Record protocol version, generated paths, and fingerprints in the manifest. Never silently overwrite user-created or user-edited managed files: compare, explain, and require confirmation; update only recognized generated files or explicitly approved managed sections.

After create or reopen, show Start your agent guidance: open a terminal in the Board Workspace and launch Copilot CLI, Claude Code, or another compatible agent. Do not fabricate a `cd` command because directory handles do not reveal portable absolute paths. Show Waiting for agent until a valid workspace-matched heartbeat arrives, then calmly show identity, control state, current turn, and heartbeat time. If absent, provide copyable fallback instructions, diagnostics, Repair agent setup, and retry. Do not promise every product/version discovers root instructions.

The skill is provider-neutral and uses only Python 3 standard library modules, including `sqlite3`, `argparse`, JSON, and filesystem APIs. It preflights Python and required modules; if unavailable, it states the exact trusted installation command and obtains approval before changing the machine. It exposes validated commands for workspace status, ready-work inspection, atomic claim/release, typed mutations, artifact publication, structured questions, answer consumption, yield, heartbeat, and watch. Mutating commands require expected revision, control generation, actor, run id, and idempotency key. Conflicts, revoked control, malformed data, and invalid transitions are explicit failures.

Use `.ai-kanban/coordination/` as a mailbox, not a second domain database. It contains a versioned human signal and one versioned state file per approved agent. Each actor solely writes its own file; all may read. Records include `workspace_id`, protocol version, actor/holder id, monotonic sequence or control generation, timestamp, requested state, and last observed durable revision. Safely replace records; ignore incomplete, stale, mismatched-workspace, or lower-generation records. Keep substantive questions, answers, progress, outputs, and audit history in SQLite.

Enforce a single acknowledged primary-file writer. Model `human`, `granting_agent`, `agent`, `reclaim_requested`, and `recovering`, with `owner`, `holder_id`, `control_generation`, `workspace_revision`, and bounded lease metadata in both SQLite and the mailbox. Every mutation rechecks generation, holder, and expected revision immediately before write. Control changes require request and acknowledgement. A requester does not write until the prior owner commits or rolls back, closes its writer, publishes its final revision, and acknowledges handoff. Human reclaim has priority: the agent completes or rolls back its short transaction, rejects later mutations, publishes yielded, and rereads before a new grant. Lease expiry is recovery evidence, never authorization to overwrite.

For direct native SQLite agent coordination, the browser flushes pending work, increments generation, grants control in SQLite, closes the writable stream, publishes grant, and becomes read-only. Before every agent mutation, open a fresh connection, use `BEGIN IMMEDIATE`, verify control/revision in both locations, mutate plus audit event, increment revision, commit, and close. Never hold a transaction during reasoning, tool execution, artifact generation, waiting, or polling. After commit, publish revision; the browser waits for journal stabilization, runs integrity check, confirms revision, reloads, and preserves selection, scroll, open detail, and unsaved drafts or flags conflicts.

The generated operating loop is explicit: poll with bounded backoff, heartbeat, atomically claim one ready turn, execute through skill commands, publish checkpoints, ask for input or complete/yield, and return to watching while the host runtime remains alive. Empty queues are quiet, not completion. A watch command is opt-in, cancellable, resumable, machine-readable, non-busy-waiting, and immediately yields on reclaim. State plainly that a skill cannot keep a terminated host runtime alive, consume future output, or initiate new model turns; where host hooks/schedulers are unavailable, watch is observation only with manual-resume guidance.

## 4. Cards, decision loops, execution turns, memory, and output surfaces

Cards are operational workspaces, not merely tickets. At creation require a title, board, column, and kind; support task, question, and result presentation. Include Markdown description, priority `P0`–`P3`, assignee, timestamps, attention state, workflow projection, dependencies, provenance, artifact paths, and last-change actor. Compact cards show title, high-value summary, priority, owner, current turn/status, latest-result preview, attention cue, and accessible actions; detail shows all metadata, history, plans, outputs, memory, provenance, and activity. Agent-changed cards show calm violet/teal plus icon and text until reviewed; Needs you uses amber plus icon and text.

Support creation, edit, duplicate where useful, archive, search, filter, sort, saved views, bulk selection, keyboard movement, pointer drag/drop, accessible drop targets, cancellation, optimistic rollback, and useful empty states. Every column has stable id, display name, order, and optional description. Surface board counts, attention, blocked, aging, WIP, ownership, and bottleneck information only when it helps decisions; avoid an operations-console aesthetic.

A turn is one bounded execution attempt against durable card intent. Claim at most one active turn per card by default, atomically with revision and idempotency validation. Initial cards may be Ready for agent and must not execute merely because a template loads. Run again/Requeue creates a fresh queued turn with new id and number, current instruction snapshot, and link to the prior successful turn; it never rewrites earlier turns. Moving completed work to Inbox confirms **Run again** and invokes this same operation. A turn needing input remains active and resumes after an answer; cancellation retains partial outputs, activity, and reason.

Each generated output belongs to a turn and has version, status, timestamps, actor, provenance, optional artifact path, and typed renderer. Render Markdown safely; show programs with language/file/copy actions, tables with schema validation/filter/export, diffs with comparison and approval, images with preview/zoom/download/alt text/provenance, files with safe open/download, and status surfaces with meaningful progress/health. Streamed output is visibly partial; failed/stale/superseded output explains recovery. Feature the latest successful result with preview, age, and Open; keep dated versions in ordered History and support turn comparison when meaningful.

The vacation decision loop is a required exemplar and product flow. In Inbox, the human edits candidate destinations and constraints. In Planning, an exploratory turn researches broad credible alternatives and produces a bounded comparison with fit, evidence, tradeoffs, uncertainty, practical constraints, and distinctions. It asks focused questions rather than guessing consequential preferences, preserves append-only rankings/shortlists/rejections/restorations/annotations, and on later passes identifies materially changed facts and ranking deltas. A deep-research gate requires explicit selected option, current constraints, and a labelled action. A confirmed Planning-to-In Progress move may atomically complete exploration and queue deep work. Deep work snapshots selection, constraints, unresolved questions, evidence, and feedback; it does not silently reconsider rejected options. It produces dated itineraries and decision-specific artifacts, then moves to Review for approval or revision. Acceptance preserves all prior proposals, feedback, turns, outputs, and provenance.

For recurring research cards, every cycle records date, cadence, lookback, exact topic, news/events mode, new findings, still-important context, source coverage, and gaps. Before a cycle, inspect prior reports and visible durable memory. Classify items as new, materially updated, unchanged context, duplicate coverage, corrected, or no longer current; distinguish confirmed fact, reported claim, announcement, opinion, forecast, and speculation. Persist only committed source-backed memory changes with lineage. Let users inspect, search, correct, dismiss, pin, export, and explicitly forget memory; forgetting changes future comparison context but not immutable reports.

## 5. Interface states and interactions

The experience is calm, capable, and trustworthy: restrained navy, mineral teal, warm paper, and coral attention accents; no global chat pane or dense operations console. Use native accessible controls, semantic landmarks, visible keyboard focus, sufficient contrast, screen-reader labels for icon-only controls, reduced-motion support, and responsive layouts down to 320 CSS pixels. The native `hidden` attribute is authoritative and CSS must not reveal inactive states.

Before activation, show Open/Create actions. Once active, show Save, New card, Agent control, AI handoff, Workspace menu, search, attention filters, folder/permission/save state, and Close workspace. Foreground Needs you, AI working, and AI updated counts without overwhelming board scanning. Provide first-run, loading, empty, active, dirty, saving, saved, conflict, unsupported-browser, permission-limited, migration, corrupt-file, recovery, and offline/static-host states with concrete next actions.

Card detail supports metadata/description editing, plan items, outputs, turns, research memory, version history, activity/provenance, structured replies to agent questions, Run again, archive, and publication of polished result cards. Activity entries are compact for routine events and expandable for decisions/errors/output updates; distinguish human, agent, system, automation, and errors calmly, show relative plus exact time, permit filters and copyable/linkable references, and avoid secrets or raw internal payloads.

AI handoff exports selected work as a compact versioned JSON and Markdown packet containing intent, constraints, plan, relevant activity, output shape, and provenance. Users copy/download it for any assistant, then import responses through paste/file selection. Validate a packet fully before preview; require approval for proposed plan, output, status, and activity changes; retain packet plus committed provenance. An optional `AIProviderAdapter` is replaceable and provider-neutral. Credentials are session-memory only, never persisted in browser storage, logs, URLs, analytics, or workspace files. Before send, disclose provider, endpoint, model, exact selected content, and purpose; require confirmation. Network failures leave the workspace unchanged with a retryable draft.

## 6. Security, compatibility, and recovery

All workspace and imported content is untrusted. Safely render Markdown and AI text; never treat it as HTML, scripts, or instructions. Validate manifests, SQLite messages, packet schemas, agent coordination records, artifact paths, external responses, and SQL parameters. External network activity requires a user action and visible destination, purpose, progress, failure, and retry state. The app does not promise secure secret storage, background execution, multi-user coordination, or autonomous service behavior in a static deployment.

Handle permission revocation, missing files, unsupported future manifests/schema, corrupt databases, partial exports, migration failure, lock failure, agent crash, stale signals, expired leases, journal residue, external mutation, agent commit without marker, and browser save conflict with specific recovery guidance. Forced recovery invalidates generation, waits for database/journal stabilization, validates integrity, explains risk, and never silently overwrites. Preserve active form drafts across reloads; present merge/reload choices when conflicts affect them.

Autosave is available only for connected supporting browsers. Elsewhere, explicit archive export/import is the persistence path. Do not silently fall back from a connected workspace to unrelated OPFS or browser storage. Keep all required JavaScript and WASM assets local and version-pinned; core behavior must not depend on mutable CDN assets.
